records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog error message is always a non-empty string (e.g. 'undefined: ...'), making the t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback dead code and exposing 'undefined:' prefixes to users
records.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler constructs `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Template literals are never falsy, so the fallback is dead code, and when err.data is undefined users see an 'undefined: <err.message>' prefix (with t() applied to a raw server error string like 'booking_not_found'). This mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar provider failure returns a 500 after the DB is mutated with no rollback and no emails sent
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.handler.ts runs prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany, then calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with no try/catch (only sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped). A throw there aborts the mutation with attendees already persisted — no rollback, no compensation. This is a real consistency/atomicity defect introduced by this diff.
